what: Real 486 hardware and a real display.
why: Every DOS result comes from headless DOSBox Staging 0.83.0 with CWSDPMI. No physical 486DX, VGA card, keyboard controller or monitor has run `FIZZ2.EXE`, and nobody has looked at its mode 13h picture on a screen. The stun stars and the shot puff were grabbed from DOSBox's window under a virtual display; the death shake, a shift of at most a pixel, has not been looked at on DOS at all.

The owner heard the cluck and the Web music in playtests on 28 October 2026 and the new Web effects on 29 October 2026 (one listener, no measurement); nobody has reported hearing the DOS music, or any sound on a real AdLib, Sound Blaster or PC speaker. The DOS checks count register writes and speaker steps, the Web checks record what a stand-in `AudioContext` is asked to play, and neither can hear. The register write timings are Fizz 1's and have not been measured here.

what: Hearing the sound effects, the menu mix, the can, the whistle and the life chime.
why: The owner listened to the new effects on the Web on 29 October 2026 and found them good ("they sound decent", and they may revisit them), and after listening on both platforms chose Fizz 1's jump, pogo and fizz shot ("the FM versions of these render weird in DOS and they sound great in Fizz 1 DOS"); one person's statements, not measurements. That remark compares the FM versions with the original Fizz 1 DOS; nobody has reported how Fizz 2's DOS build sounds with Fizz 1 DOS's data in place, and nobody has reported listening to the music under Paused and Options (the Web low-pass at 900 Hz and 0.7 gain, and its approximation on DOS with operator levels) or to the soda can's fsssht, the walk-off whistle or the elixir's life chime. The Web checks record which oscillators a stand-in `AudioContext` is asked to play, and the DOS checks count register writes and speaker steps in DOSBox; neither can hear. The FM voices that remain (the alternates and the other effects) are authored by their numbers and downmixed by a best-effort mapping that was not compared by ear.

what: The oblique look and the frame budget on real screens and a real 486.
why: The oblique ground and the night sky (#142 to #146, merged) were looked at as host renders and in DOSBox and headless Chromium grabs, and judged by frame digests; no playtest of the stack is recorded. Their DOS cost is DOSBox at a fixed 26,800 cycles a millisecond (draw 9,801 us on average, six captions 12,656 us, from CI) and callgrind instruction counts on the DOS build's code; nothing was timed on a 486 or on a slow browser, and the Auto sky thresholds come from arithmetic on those figures.

DOSBox runs `/BENCH` and the sound cases at a fixed 26,800 cycles a millisecond and the other checks at `cycles=max`, charging the x87 like any simple instruction. `tools/cyc486.py` (#169), ported from Fizz 1's DOS port, estimates the drawing in 486 clocks from the datasheet's cache-hit timings and puts the x87 at about 1% of it; it leaves out cache misses, bus and VGA wait states and x87 overlap, does not cover the rules' step or the 560 Hz interrupt, and has not been compared with a real 486.

what: The Web page played by a person.
why: Headless Chromium loads the page, plays the replay's keys through the DevTools protocol and takes the screenshots. The owner played the Web build in a playtest on 28 October 2026 and found the HUD good (that was the first HUD; the Two-Row Stack has been looked at in screenshots only); the playtest notes do not cover fullscreen, Keyboard Lock, touch or a screen reader, and Firefox, Safari and a phone have not loaded the page.

what: The DOS build in a browser.
why: The local preview site (#175) runs `FIZZ2.EXE` in js-dos 8.5.3; muted headless Chromium booted `/LIVE`, `/CHECK` and the help screen there. Nobody has listened to its sound, its timing follows the host, and it is not part of any check.

The twenty-two traces are committed and Fizz 2 matches them bit for bit, but CI never runs `tools/fizz1-trace`, so nothing regenerates the files from Fizz 1 on its own. The four wall-kick traces were written from Fizz 1 at `9729c07` with the pinned-commit check bypassed. `tools/lf-sim-drift.sh` was run by hand against a Fizz 1 checkout.

what: Bundling the Web build into a launcher.
why: `dist/web` uses relative URLs so a launcher can host it under any path; no launcher has.

what: The GitHub runner, beyond the runs recorded.
why: CI passed on the head commit of each pull request and on the merge commits listed in the evidence tables ({{m.ciGreen}} merged pull requests green on main). A run not listed there has not been seen. The first full run on main after the soda can merged (#127) failed once in the parallel replay of a corrupt `FIZZ2.CFG`, and a re-run of the same commit passed; the cause is unknown and the case is a watch item, and since #130 a failing case prints its last 30 lines. The nightly full gate passed on each of its five runs from 1 to 5 November 2026 (`gh run list --event schedule`).

what: Other DPMI hosts and DOS versions.
why: Only CWSDPMI under DOSBox's own DOS. FreeDOS, MS-DOS, EMM386 and HDPMI are untried, and the FreeDOS-bootable floppy has not been built. Whether FreeDOS's `COMMAND.COM` passes `/?` through to the program is unchecked.
